name: Admin Accounting Income Client Link
description: Superuser links each income to the client it came from at /panel/accounting/incomes. The income form carries a searchable client picker (with inline client creation) and an Origen control for the business line (desarrollo/hosting/diagnostico/otro); the client is optional, so a refund or a financial yield can stay unassigned. The table shows a Cliente column, the filter panel gains Cliente (options derived from the loaded rows plus a "Sin cliente" sentinel) and Origen filters, and a "Sin cliente" builtin tab isolates the rows still to be completed. Those rows are completed in bulk from the shared ClientBulkAssignBar, the same component /panel/accounting/hostings uses: checkboxes select rows (or every filtered row) and The bulk bar holds only the selection count and one [Acciones] menu; Asignar cliente and Asignar proyecto open BulkAssignModal (picker + live plan + gated confirm), Desvincular cliente and Quitar proyecto go straight to the confirmation, and Registrar abono opens its own modal. The menu opens upward (the bar is sticky at the bottom) and separates linking from collecting with a divider; Headless UI only renders the panel while it is open, so an action being absent or disabled is only observable with the menu open. "Asignar cliente" opens the modal, whose confirm stays disabled while no client is picked with the reason on the line right beside it — an empty picker no longer means unlink — and "Desvincular cliente" only appears in the menu when a selected row actually has a client. Either way the scope is named before anything is written: how many rows gain a client, how many change one and from which client (a mixed selection is broken down instead of presented as a single operation), plus the full scrollable list of affected records. Only the rows that actually change travel in POST /api/accounting/incomes/bulk-assign-client/ (one audit entry per income), and the toast afterwards reports how many the server really wrote. A "Totales por cliente" modal breaks the FILTERED incomes down into billed / collected / pending / weight per client with a totals row, so the period comes from the active filters. Settling an income carries its client and origin into the liquid child, and a client holding incomes can no longer be deleted. The list can also render GROUPED BY CLIENT: the backend setting income_default_view_mode (edited in Configuración) decides the landing mode on every visit, the in-page Agrupado/Clásico segmented toggle lasts only the session (nothing persists on the device), and the grouped table shows per-client headers over the whole filtered set with a trailing 'Sin cliente' bucket flagged 'por completar' and billed/collected/pending footer totals. Each group header reads as ONE UNIT at the start of the row: the client name with its record count and, contiguous to it, Facturado, Pendiente and Participación en lo facturado — each its own block with the label above the value in smaller muted type, so the name keeps the visual weight. That two-line block is what made the figures legible; spreading them across the width of the row was tried and rejected, because on a wide table the amounts landed far enough from the name to read as columns of something else again. The separation between the three blocks is uniform and compact with no separators (each already carries its own label), and the name and its count are centred against the two-line blocks. A long client name yields space and ellipsizes instead of pushing a figure out of the row or breaking one in half; the amounts never compress. The footer takes the same treatment, so the table reads the same way top to bottom — it keeps the order Facturado, Pendiente, Cobrado — which costs the vertical alignment between rows on purpose, since every name measures differently. Both amounts always render, zero included; the share label states what the figure IS (the group's part of the billed total, not how much of the group is billed); and below sm the blocks drop together to a second line under the name without stretching or breaking. Since Ago 2026 the grouped view also carries the selection: a checkbox per row, one per client group that ticks or clears the whole group and reads indeterminate while only part of it is selected, and a header 'seleccionar todos' spanning every group — with no pagination here, that is exactly the filtered set. A collapsed group states how many of its rows are selected, because they keep counting towards the bulk action; the selection lives on the page, so it survives switching between Agrupado and Clásico; and the same ClientBulkAssignBar drives the same two actions, now sticky at the bottom (incomes and hostings alike) and flagging '· N fuera del filtro actual' when part of the selection no longer passes the active filters — the action still includes those rows and the confirmation lists them. Column sort and pagination stay classic-only. A 'Sin cliente' KPI card (without_client_count, whole filtered set) surfaces the completion debt, the search box also matches the linked client's name/company (server-side q included), each unassigned row in the classic table wears a 'sin vincular' pill, reassigning an expected's client cascades to its settled liquids, and the cuenta de cobro adopts the client on an orphan income or rejects a mismatched one. (Ago 2026) The selection is reconciled against the records that still exist: deleting a selected income drops that id on its own — only that one, so a partial deletion of a multi-selection keeps the rest — the count and the '· N fuera del filtro actual' notice recompute over real rows, and the bar hides itself once nothing is left to assign, with no reload and no Cancelar. If part of the batch was deleted while the confirmation was open, POST bulk-assign-client/ answers 409 records_not_found naming missing_ids and writes nothing; the panel drops those ids and reloads. The client-assignment modal focuses the filter on open and immediately renders a permanent catalog instead of reserving an empty dropdown gap: at least five complete client rows fit before the catalog itself scrolls, while the modal and its review pane stay fixed. Each row identifies the client by name, company and email and flags a missing email. The filter narrows the visible rows without hiding the catalog; an unmatched filter explains the empty state and opens inline client creation. Name sorting starts A-Z, toggles to Z-A from the Nombre header and persists across later openings. The selected-record count and names are already visible before a client is chosen, desktop height follows the content, and compact screens use the full viewport.
